title: Consistency models, CAP, PACELC, ACID vs BASE, transactions, isolation levels
relevance: High — almost every HLD "design X" round probes C vs A tradeoffs, when to use strong vs eventual consistency, and ACID/isolation for money/inventory paths (campus + experienced; FAANG and Indian product cos).
company_notes: Campus/new-grad HLD expects CAP and strong-vs-eventual vocabulary on shorteners, feeds, chat, e-commerce, with isolation depth separating strong candidates. Mid-level (1–4+ YOE) probes per-API consistency, PACELC latency tradeoffs, isolation anomalies, and saga vs 2PC at Amazon, Google, Meta, Uber, Atlassian, Flipkart, and payments-heavy loops. Near-universal whenever designs replicate or handle money/inventory.

phases.goal: Establish CAP under partition, that CAP C ≠ ACID C, PACELC’s normal-path tradeoff, and what ACID vs BASE mean.

must_hit.point: Under a network partition in a distributed store, you must choose Consistency (every read sees the latest write or errors) vs Availability (every non-failed node answers, maybe stale); CA without P is not a real distributed design.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States partitions happen and names the C vs A forced choice; rejects “pick CA and ignore P.”

must_hit.point: CAP consistency ≈ linearizability / single-copy recency; ACID consistency = preserve application invariants (constraints, balances ≥ 0)—never conflate them.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates “latest replica view” from “invariants still hold,” ideally with a money or constraint example.

must_hit.point: PACELC: if Partition → Availability vs Consistency; Else (healthy) → Latency vs Consistency; most of the time there is no partition, so sync replication buys stronger C at higher latency.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites P→A/C and E→L/C and notes the healthy-path latency tax.

must_hit.point: ACID: Atomic all-or-nothing, Consistent invariants, Isolated concurrent txns, Durable after commit; BASE (Basically Available, Soft state, Eventually consistent) favors availability/scale and requires tolerating temporary divergence plus compensating logic.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists A/C/I/D clearly and contrasts BASE as availability-oriented, not a theorem.

probes: In a distributed database, what does CAP force you to choose during a partition, and how is CAP’s “C” different from ACID’s “C”?

hints.1: Start from “partition happens”—what do non-failed nodes do vs what do readers see?
hints.2: Map CAP C to linearizable recency and ACID C to invariants; then name PACELC’s Else branch.
hints.3: Under P: Consistency (latest-or-error) vs Availability (answer, maybe stale). CAP C ≠ ACID C (invariants). PACELC Else: Latency vs Consistency.

phases.goal: Walk the replica consistency spectrum, isolation levels and anomalies, linearizability vs serializability, and why 2PC is costly.

must_hit.point: Replica consistency spectrum: strong/linearizable (read always latest) → causal (cause before effect) → read-your-writes/session → eventual (replicas converge if writes stop); pick per data item/API.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Orders the spectrum and says choice is per API/item, not a whole-DB slogan.

must_hit.point: Isolation weak→strong: Read Uncommitted → Read Committed → Repeatable Read / Snapshot → Serializable; phenomena include dirty read, non-repeatable read, phantom, and write skew (classic SI hole—two doctors both go off-call).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the level ladder and at least dirty/non-repeatable/phantom plus write skew with a concrete sketch.

must_hit.point: Linearizability = single-object real-time order; serializability = multi-object txn order as if one-at-a-time; you can have one without the other; strict serializability is both.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts single-object real-time vs multi-object as-if-serial and mentions strict serializability as both.

must_hit.point: 2PC/distributed txns give atomic commit across nodes but coordinator failure can block; prefer single-partition ACID or saga/outbox over cross-shard 2PC unless truly needed.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names blocking coordinator risk and defaults to single-partition or saga/outbox.

probes: Walk the consistency spectrum for replicas, then sketch dirty read, non-repeatable read, phantom, and write skew—and say which isolation stops write skew.

hints.1: Think “what can a reader see after a write” and “what can two concurrent transactions see.”
hints.2: Spectrum: linearizable → causal → read-your-writes → eventual. Isolation ladder ends at Serializable/SSI for write skew.
hints.3: Write skew is the SI hole (e.g. two doctors off-call); Serializable/SSI stops it. Linearizability ≠ serializability; 2PC can block on coordinator failure.

phases.goal: Frame CP vs AP per feature, PACELC latency vs consistency when healthy, and when strong C beats eventual.

must_hit.point: Do not label whole DBs “CP/AP”; real systems mix modes—prefer “for this API, under this failure, we choose …”.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Refuses Mongo/Cassandra/Postgres as a single CAP letter; scopes to operation and failure mode.

must_hit.point: Under no partition, async primary–replica vs sync quorum trades Latency vs Consistency (PACELC ELC); strong consistency has a latency tax even when healthy (sync replication / quorum R+W>N).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties healthy-path sync/quorum to higher latency for stronger C and mentions R+W>N or sync replication.

must_hit.point: Design rule: money/inventory/unique booking → strong C + careful isolation; feeds, counts, profiles, CDN/DNS-like data → availability + eventual (plus read-your-writes where UX demands).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Splits money/booking paths from feed/profile/CDN-like paths with matching consistency choices.

must_hit.point: CAP forbids perfect C and perfect A during a partition, not “mostly consistent and mostly available.”
must_hit.evidence_hint: Corrects the cartoon triangle: partial C/A and latency matter; perfect C+A under partition is what CAP rules out.

probes: For a ticket marketplace, which of browse, reserve seat, pay, and popularity counter lean CP vs AP—and under no partition, what does async vs sync replication trade?

hints.1: Ask what a wrong answer costs the user for each feature.
hints.2: Reserve/pay need strong C; browse/popularity can lean AP/eventual; healthy path is L vs C.
hints.3: Seat reserve and pay: CP-leaning / strong C. Browse and popularity: AP-leaning / eventual. Async replicas: lower latency, weaker C; sync quorum: stronger C, higher latency.

phases.goal: Apply consistency choices to concrete paths: transfers, profile UX, checkout vs replicas, and distributed money without 2PC.

must_hit.point: Transfer ₹100 A→B needs Atomicity and Durability; distinguish invariant consistency from replica recency; Read Committed alone can leave race/isolation bugs on concurrent money paths.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses the transfer example to separate atomic/durable commit, invariant C, and why weak isolation is unsafe for concurrent updates.

must_hit.point: Profile-pic style update: read-your-writes for the writer, eventual for others; causal consistency matters when comments-on-posts must respect cause-before-effect.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives session/RYW for the updater and eventual for others; links causal to comment/post ordering.

must_hit.point: Read replicas are eventually consistent by default—never serve checkout/balance from a lagging replica without sticky/primary reads.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly bans checkout/balance off async replicas unless reading primary or sticky to fresh data.

must_hit.point: Two services (wallet, ledger): prefer saga/outbox + idempotency over XA/2PC; handle at-least-once duplicates as a failure mode.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Outlines compensating saga or outbox with idempotent handlers and names duplicate delivery.

probes: Walk a ₹100 wallet transfer and a wallet+ledger design without 2PC—where do you need strong isolation, and what breaks if checkout reads a lagging replica?

hints.1: Separate “commit survived” from “both sides stay consistent under concurrency.”
hints.2: Primary/sticky reads for checkout; saga/outbox + idempotency instead of XA.
hints.3: ACID on the money path; Read Committed races; replicas lag so checkout uses primary; cross-service: saga/outbox, handle duplicate at-least-once.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: When the network partitions, every non-failed node either refuses/stales for Consistency or keeps answering for Availability; CA without P is not a viable distributed design.
Most of the time there is no partition: sync replication or quorum (R+W>N) buys stronger consistency at a latency tax; async replicas lower latency but risk stale reads.

tradeoffs.topic: Strong consistency + isolation vs availability + eventual
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Money, inventory, and unique booking take strong C and careful isolation; feeds, counts, profiles, and CDN/DNS-like data take availability and eventual consistency, with read-your-writes where UX needs it.
Prefer single-partition ACID or saga/outbox with idempotency; 2PC gives cross-node atomic commit but coordinator failure can block, so use it only when truly required.

gotchas.trap: Calling Cassandra “AP” and Postgres “CP” as the whole story
gotchas.correction: Too coarse—ask which operation, which consistency setting, and which failure (node vs datacenter partition); systems mix modes.
Replicas converge if writes stop; you still need conflict resolution (LWW, version vectors, app merges).

gotchas.trap: Assuming strong consistency is free when the network is healthy
gotchas.correction: PACELC’s ELC: sync replication / quorum still costs latency even without a partition.
Postgres defaults to Read Committed; MySQL InnoDB often Repeatable Read—race bugs hide until load.

gotchas.trap: Serving checkout or balance from a default read replica
gotchas.correction: Replicas are eventually consistent by default; use sticky/primary reads for money paths.

gotchas.trap: Reading CAP as forbidding any mix of consistency and availability
gotchas.correction: CAP forbids perfect C and perfect A during a partition; systems can still be mostly consistent and mostly available.
